# Overview

The Ontario Special Investigations Unit (SIU) publishes director's
reports on police-civilian interactions within its mandate (death,
serious injury, sexual assault, or the discharge of a firearm at a
person). rmorie has a pipeline for that corpus:

- `morie_fetch_siu()`, which writes the panel-reviewed corpus bundled
  in rmoriedata or, on request, fetches the reports live;
- a C++ parser for the English and French report templates;
- a language-aware DRID manifest that ships inside the package
  (`morie_siu_index()`);
- a correction system that applies hand-verified values over the
  parser output (`morie_siu_record_correction()`);
- audit and LLM tooling (`morie_siu_audit_case()`,
  `morie_siu_anomaly_check()`, `morie_siu_llm_extract()`,
  `morie_siu_compare()`) and French-to-English translation
  (`morie_siu_translate()`).

Chunks marked `eval = FALSE` below need the network or a running LLM
server, and are not run when the vignette is built.

# Inspecting the shipped manifest

The DRID manifest ships inside the package, so reading it requires no
network access.

```{r manifest}
library(rmorie)

manifest <- morie_siu_index()
dim(manifest)
table(manifest$`_language`)

# canonical_drid points each French drid at its English counterpart.
head(manifest[manifest$`_language` == "fr",
              c("drid", "case_number", "canonical_drid")])
```

# The corpus

`morie_fetch_siu()` returns the path of an SIU.csv file. By default it
writes the panel-reviewed corpus from rmoriedata:

```{r corpus}
csv_path <- morie_fetch_siu(lang = "en")
siu <- utils::read.csv(csv_path, colClasses = "character")
dim(siu)
```

With `options(morie.siu.allow_fetch = TRUE)` the function fetches the
reports live instead. It walks the manifest, requests each report and
news release through a rate-limited pool (`rate_rps` requests per
second, `concurrency` parallel transfers, up to 3 retries per request),
interleaving the report and news-release requests, and parses the
pages with the C++ parser:

```{r fetch, eval = FALSE}
options(morie.siu.allow_fetch = TRUE)
csv_path <- morie_fetch_siu(
  lang       = "en",   # skip French drids: half the network traffic
  cache_html = TRUE,   # keep the pages locally for audits and re-runs
  rate_rps   = 4,      # requests per second
  overwrite  = TRUE
)
```

# Auditing a single case

`morie_siu_audit_case()` returns the parser row, the raw report and
news HTML, and the cleaned text side by side, so you can see exactly
what the parser saw. It fetches the pages if they are not cached:

```{r audit, eval = FALSE}
audit <- morie_siu_audit_case("17-OVI-201")
names(audit)
# "row" "drid" "nrid" "report_html" "news_html" "report_text" "news_text"
```

`morie_siu_anomaly_check()` asks an LLM, per field, whether the HTML
supports the parsed value, and `morie_siu_audit_columns()` does the
same across a sample of cases. Both need an LLM provider (see below):

```{r anomaly, eval = FALSE}
morie_siu_anomaly_check("17-OVI-201")
morie_siu_audit_columns(case_numbers = sample(siu$case_number, 50))
```

# Comparing parser output against an external table

`morie_siu_compare()` produces a side-by-side diff between the parser
row and any external table that names the same case. `field_map` maps
external column names to parser field names, and `external_case_col`
names the external table's case-number column:

```{r compare, eval = FALSE}
my_other_table <- data.frame(
  case_number = "17-OVI-201",
  n_officers  = 1L
)

morie_siu_compare(
  case_number       = "17-OVI-201",
  external          = my_other_table,
  field_map         = c(n_officers = "number_of_subject_officials"),
  external_case_col = "case_number"
)
```

# LLM extraction

`morie_siu_llm_extract()` runs an LLM over a cached report and returns
the parser's 64 columns as extracted by the model. The default
`model = c("ollama", "route", "gemini")` tries a local Ollama server
first, then the model configured with `morie_llm_config()`, then
Gemini (paid, `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`). A local Ollama
server needs no API key.

```{r llm, eval = FALSE}
morie_siu_llm_extract("17-OVI-201", model = "ollama")
```

Ollama settings: `OLLAMA_HOST` (default `http://localhost:11434`),
`OLLAMA_MODEL` (otherwise the first model the server lists), and
`OLLAMA_API_KEY` for hosted gateways.

# French -> English translation

`morie_siu_translate()` translates the text fields
(`narrative_summary`, `news_release_summary`, `news_release_title`,
`relevant_legislation`) of cached French reports through the LLM
provider:

```{r translate, eval = FALSE}
morie_siu_translate(target_lang = "en", case_numbers = "17-OVI-201")
```

# Corrections: the parser learns

Ship-time corrections live in
`inst/extdata/siu_canonical_overrides.csv.gz`:

```{r overrides}
ov <- utils::read.csv(system.file("extdata", "siu_canonical_overrides.csv.gz",
                                  package = "rmorie"))
nrow(ov)                       # corrections
length(unique(ov$case_number)) # cases they cover
```

Users can add their own corrections, which take effect on the next
`morie_fetch_siu()` run:

```{r override, eval = FALSE}
morie_siu_record_correction(
  case_number    = "17-OVI-201",
  field          = "number_of_officers_involved",
  verified_value = "1",
  note           = "checked against the report"
)
```

Overrides are applied per cell, by case number, immediately after the
parser writes its initial output.

# Format validity

`morie_siu_sanity_check()` validates per-row format constraints:
case-number pattern, ISO dates, integer counts, Yes / No values, and
narrative columns that are empty or suspiciously short. It expects the
columns as character, so read the CSV with `colClasses = "character"`
(as above):

```{r sanity}
sane <- morie_siu_sanity_check(siu)
sum(sane$issues_count > 0)   # rows with at least one flag
head(sort(table(unlist(strsplit(sane$issues[sane$issues_count > 0], ";"))),
          decreasing = TRUE))
```
